collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — JUSTICE AND CONSEQUENCES (JUS-01 to JUS-50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Everyday rules, disputes between neighbors, the elders and the council, making things right, losing a role, a night to cool down, wrongful suspicion and evidence that doesn't add up. Consequences are proportionate and never cruel; children get guidance; nobody goes without food, water or shelter; an accusation is not guilt.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: Two teens learning to fish argued until they tipped the canoe: put them in different canoes, or give them one job together.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) and (friend) are learning to fish with the same group of adults, and they argue about everything, loudly, every single day: who paddles, who holds the net, who scared the fish away. This morning their argument tipped the canoe over in the shallows, and the morning's catch went with it. The fishers have asked the elders what to do.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The elders put them in different canoes for one moon. Both of them are offended. Within a week, both of them are quietly relieved. At the end of the moon they are put back together, and argue about everything again, but a little less loudly, and the canoe stays the right way up.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The elders give them one canoe, one net and one task: catch enough for the elders' supper between the two of them, and come back only when they have. It takes them all day. They argue for most of it. They paddle in at sunset with exactly enough fish, sunburned and grudgingly pleased with themselves.
